title: Somebody Sang It to Me
sketch: C: lullaby. The singer weighs every other way to keep something (a mind, a page, numbers, a screen) and sings it instead; rocking 3/4 in a plain major.
refrain: No-bo-dy wrote it and no-bo-dy owns it;
I'll sing it to you, and you'll sing it to some-one,

lines: I could have [kept it in a vehicle],
verse_template.note: The last verse answers why it was sung instead.

hooks.why: 'nobody' rising, then 'nobody' falling from the octave
the climb to the ninth on 'sing it to someone'

seed_verses: I could have kept it a-lone in my head,
safe as a stone in a well;
down it would go when I went to my rest,
no-bo-dy left who could tell.
I could have writ-ten it down on a page,
fold-ed and put on a shelf;
pa-per will yel-low and lan-guage will change
till it is strange to it-self.
I could have saved it as num-bers and light,
cop-ied as quick as a wink;
bright as it is, when the pow-er goes out,
dark-er than wa-ter or ink.
I could have shown it to all of the world,
lit up in ev-ery-one's hand;
ev-ery-one watch-es and no-bo-dy sings,
gone like a print in the sand.
So I just sang it the way that it came,
hummed it with-out all the words;
songs need no pa-per or pow-er or name,
on-ly a mouth, like the birds.
